title: Desk Guidance — Contribution Hold on Credit Balance Refunds after Late Payment Interest
content:
**Rule applied at the desk.** On the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts, a contribution hold is taken off a credit balance refund as a share of the most recent contribution assessment booked from an original report. The share follows the late payment interest entries booked on the account within the payment record months, 12:

| Late payment interest entries booked within 12 months | Share of the latest original-report assessment held |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 1.0 — the whole assessment |
| Exactly one | 0.5 |
| None | Nothing is held |

- **Window.** The 12 months are counted in whole months back from the day of the request, by the entry dates of the interest entries in the account's balance history.
- **Assessment used.** The contribution assessment with the latest entry date among those booked from an original report; assessments resting on an estimate or on an amended report are not used.
- **Where the hold is taken.** Off the refundable amount after any share kept back from the credit balance; what is left after the hold is never below zero.

## Points of judgement (hypothetical, latest original-report assessment USD 1,039.60, refundable amount before the hold USD 939.06)

| Interest entries in 12 months | Hold | Left after the hold |
|---|---|---|
| None | 0.00 | 939.06 |
| One | 519.80 | 419.26 |
| Two | 1,039.60 | 0.00 (never below zero) |
| Three, of which one booked 15 months before the request | 1,039.60 (two in the window) | 0.00 |
